predecessors.note: Mirrors the Beylik entry in regency-of-algiers successors. The page's infobox 'Established: 1528' dates the beylik as a province of Algiers; it is drawn inside the Regency (and the Cliopatria Ottoman row) until Algiers fell in 1830, and as a state of its own from then on (see notes).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the gazetteer's Constantinois plus Béjaïa and Biskra provinces stand for the beylik. The page gives its dimensions, 'approximately 430 km in its greatest length and 330 km in average width' (about 142,000 km2 if it were a rectangle), against the shape's 89,800 km2 (ratio 0.63); the page has no infobox area. The Béjaïa end is the page's 'from Béjaïa to Annaba'; the western limit (the Beylik of Titteri) is not placed by the page.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Béjaïa leaves in 1833 ('in 1833 France captured the city with minimal losses, from Kabyle and Kouloughli forces'). The page does not call the defenders the Bey's; the Beylik page puts Béjaïa inside the province, so the disc (35 km, as in french-algeria ledger 2) is taken from it; french-algeria ledger 2 gives nobody as the counterpart. The shape holds to the Beylik's fall in 1837.

region.text: the province of Constantine, from Béjaïa to Annaba and the Sahara fringe

ledger.note: 1830: the Constantinians rally to Ahmed Bey after Algiers falls. 'After the capture of Algiers by the French in 1830, the Constantinians invested power in Ahmed Bey, who organized the fight against the French troops.' The infobox (Established 1528, 'Provincial governorate', 'Elective monarchy under the suzerainty of the Algerian Dey') makes it a province of the Regency until then; the page gives no month for the investiture, and Algiers fell on 5 July 1830 (regency-of-algiers ledger).

1832: the French occupy Bône. The Annaba page has Ottoman rule 'lasted until French occupation in 1832' (no month; 'Rule by the Ottoman Empire began in 1533'); the Beylik page names Annaba the second city of the province after Constantine. Mirror of french-algeria ledger 1.

1833: Bougie falls to France. 'in 1833 France captured the city with minimal losses, from Kabyle and Kouloughli forces'; the Beylik page has the province's coast running 'from Béjaïa to Annaba'. The page does not say the defenders were the Bey's, hence confidence 2, and french-algeria ledger 2 records nobody as the counterpart.

1837: Constantine falls. 'It took two sieges to overcome the resistance of the inhabitants of the city, which fell in 1837'; Clauzel's 8,700 men were 'repulsed' in November 1836 and Damrémont, killed in the siege, was 'replaced by Sylvain Charles, comte Valée' (French conquest page). The day, 13 October 1837, is french-algeria ledger 8's reading of the French Algeria page, not opened here.

ledger.note: 1837: the Beylik of Constantine ends with the fall of its capital. 'The Beylik collapsed in the 1837 siege of Constantine during the French conquest of Algeria'; 'The Constantine department was formed upon the bases of the Beylik in 1848'. The page gives no end date for Ahmed Bey's resistance in the Aurès beyond his surrender in 1848.

wars.name: Sieges of Constantine
wars.outcome: French victory at the second attempt: Clauzel's expedition of November 1836 was repulsed; the city fell in 1837, Damrémont having been killed and replaced by Valée. The Beylik collapsed.
wars.note: 'In November 1836 Clausel led 8,700 men into the Constantine beylik, but was repulsed'; 'the failure led to Clausel's recall'. The Beylik page: 'It took two sieges to overcome the resistance of the inhabitants of the city, which fell in 1837.' Ahmed Bey's guerrilla in the Aurès to 1848 is page-silent in the conquest article.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the page gives the province's dimensions and its neighbours (Tunis on the east, Titteri on the west, the Sahara on the south) but no frontier.

notes: No Cliopatria row exists for the Beylik; its land is drawn inside Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire row (1560-1705) and Regency of Algiers row (1706-1830), then inside French Algeria. Three pages opened. Decision: the state is drawn from 1830, not from the infobox's 1528, because until Algiers fell the Bey governed a province under the Dey (the Beylik page: 'Elective monarchy under the suzerainty of the Algerian Dey'; 'Provincial governorate') and regency-of-algiers lists the Beylik as its successor; the earlier life (Hafsids of Béjaïa in the infobox as predecessor, the break from Hafsid Béjaïa 'in the early 16th century', attachment to Algiers 'in the 1530s', beys from Hasan Bou Kemia 1713 and Salah Bey 1771-1792) is page-dated only in centuries and is left to a possible province-level pass. Not settled: (1) the day of Constantine's fall (13 October 1837 on the French Algeria page cited by french-algeria ledger 8) was not on any page opened; (2) Ahmed Bey's holdout in the Aurès until 1848 is drawn as nothing, because no page gives land; (3) french-algeria ledger 2 takes Bougie from nobody, this dossier from the Beylik, and french-algeria ledger 13 names the 1840 land nobody's, so the Beylik's western and southern reach is a disagreement between dossiers; (4) the Annaba page does not mention the Beylik; Ibrahim Bey of Bône and Yusuf's 1832 capture are not on the pages opened; (5) the Béjaïa and Biskra provinces are added to the gazetteer's Constantinois (which already holds Sétif, Batna, Tébessa and Khenchela) because the page names Béjaïa and Biskra as nuba cities of the province.
